summary: This is an excerpt from a fiction work labeled 'Book 1 — part 166' in which two characters, Ange and the narrator, prepare to go on the run. The narrator receives a message from M1k3y and texts Masha about meeting tomorrow. Ange packs a ballistic nylon courier bag with minimal clothing, toiletries, and an encrypted hard-drive image she emails to herself via a neighbor's WiFi, while the narrator reflects on the weight of packs and the possibility of not returning home. The passage ends with the two of them about to continue their plans.
one_line: Ange and the narrator pack light and prepare to go fugitive, emailing encrypted data and planning to meet Masha and M1k3y the next day.
key_facts: M1k3y sends a message promising that what they are going to do is 'the most fun you will have all year, guaranteed.'
The narrator sends Masha a short message saying 'Tomorrow.'
Ange plans to carry three t-shirts, a pair of pants, a pair of shorts, three changes of underwear, three pairs of socks and a sweater.
Ange says you should never take more than three days' worth of clothes because you can rinse stuff out in the sink.
Ange packs her clothes into a ballistic nylon courier bag that goes across her chest and slings diagonally across her back.
Ange plans to stick her toothbrush in tomorrow morning before heading down to Civic Center.
The narrator says that every ounce carried adds crushing force over a million steps.
Ange asks whether to bring her Xbox, which holds notes, sketches and email on its hard-drive.
The narrator advises leaving the Xbox behind because there will be plenty of them in LA.
The narrator tells Ange to create a Pirate Party account and email an image of her hard-drive to herself.
The narrator says the hard-drive is encrypted, as is standard with ParanoidXbox.
The email transfer is expected to take a couple of hours through her neighbor's WiFi network and reach Sweden.
Ange tightens the compression straps and the bag is described as roughly the size of a soccer-ball.
Ange puts condoms inside the bag, taking them from her bedside table.
